review.summary: Attempt 2 of the phase-governance chunk is a substantive, well-evidenced response to attempt 1: all seven prior findings are addressed with real code, sensitive tests and documentation. commands_for(21) now carries the vendor-YAML whitespace exclusion (tools/check_phase.py:108), test_ci.py plus every manifest-consuming generator/oracle (check_phase.py:132-140), and a tightly scoped planning-fixture gate (verify_planning_fixture, check_phase.py:79-102) that allows only provenance.sha256/manifestSha256 to rebind while the rest of the frozen SDK stays diff-locked to 0a213fe79c. check_evidence now rejects any report carrying the contracts-only scope marker (review_phase.py:200), closing the receipt-substitution hole for phase 21 where ci_commands_for(21) still equals commands_for(21). Failed invocations now write a sanitized .failed.json receipt that verify_attempt_sequence accepts as a consumed attempt with prompt/check hash binding (review_phase.py:89-105, 523-529), ending the dead-end; SCOPE_BOUND_PHASES is hoisted (review_phase.py:17) and gate_decision takes the phase so the phase-21 >=9/10 plan floor and the recorded decision agree (review_phase.py:69-71). docs/PHASES.md:157-188 documents the recovery path, the explicit "not remote CI coverage for phases 21-23" boundary and the single SDK-file exception. The recorded evidence is real and complete: the attempt-02 snapshot lists exactly the 23 commands of commands_for(21) in order, every exit_code is 0 with timeout false, passed/source_unchanged true, bound to reviewed source a428384348e6..., with a fresh private-material receipt at the same hash. One high defect remains, and it is the same class attempt 1 raised: the exclusion was added to the new phase-21-25 lists but not to the reused release-range check that remote CI actually executes. commands_for(17)[0] (`git diff --check b65f3c9..HEAD -- . :(exclude)portkey/*.yaml`) is inherited by commands_for(20) and survives ci_commands_for(20), which the pinned workflow runs (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73); contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/mp-openapi.yaml has 46 trailing-whitespace lines and is a new file, so the first push of this branch will fail the gate AGENTS.md:13 requires, contradicting docs/PHASES.md:171-176 and docs/CI.md:141-146. Secondary: the new failed-attempt receipt makes the attempt-five relaxed gate (>40 instead of >=46 for a phase) reachable after four invocation failures and only one substantive review, with no test covering that path. Categories 8/9/8/8/8 = 41/50, below the 42 chunk floor, and the high finding blocks acceptance independently.

findings.description: The release-range whitespace check `git diff --check b65f3c9..HEAD -- . :(exclude)contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/*.yaml` is inherited verbatim by commands_for(20) (check_phase.py:175-183) and is not filtered by ci_commands_for (check_phase.py:613-616), so it is part of the 41-command subset the pinned workflow executes (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73, docs/CI.md:162-164, and it appears as the first command of docs/checks/phase-20-contracts.json:9-17). contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/mp-openapi.yaml contains 46 lines matching [ \t]+$ (verified by direct search) and is a new file (staged, not yet committed), so once this branch's commits enter b65f3c9..HEAD every added line with trailing whitespace is a whitespace error and the command exits nonzero. This is the exact precedent already encoded for the two earlier vendored YAMLs (check_phase.py:220 for Portkey, 264 for dp-openapi.yaml) and documented at docs/CI.md:141-146, which lists only those two exclusions. Consequences: the remote CI gate AGENTS.md:13 requires before pushing ordinary commits will fail for every phase-21 commit, and docs/PHASES.md:171-176 ("The unchanged remote workflow continues to qualify its historical phase20 scope until Phase24") becomes false. The attempt-01 fix was applied only to the new phase-21-25 lists (check_phase.py:108), which do not include any ranged check. Note that commands_for(17)/(20) cannot simply be edited: review_phase.check_evidence compares phase-20's accepted checks snapshot against commands_for(20), and validate_predecessors re-verifies it, so changing the full list would invalidate accepted phase-20 evidence.
findings.required_fix: Extend only the CI subset: in ci_commands_for, append ":(exclude)contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/*.yaml" (adding "--", "." when absent) to every `git diff --check` command that carries a commit range, leaving commands_for(17)/(20) byte-identical so accepted phase-20 check evidence stays valid; add a tools/test_ci.py assertion that the executed CI subset excludes each byte-pinned vendor YAML; and record the third exclusion in docs/CI.md:141-146 and the CI boundary paragraph in docs/PHASES.md:171-176. Alternatively route CI to the active phase's contracts subset and update docs/CI.md, docs/RELEASE.md and test_ci.py in lockstep, amending docs/PHASES.md:150.

findings.description: verify_attempt_sequence now accepts a .failed.json receipt in place of a completed record for any earlier attempt (lines 93-105), which correctly ends the dead-end but also makes the attempt-five exception reachable without four substantive reviews. gate_decision (lines 82-85) relaxes the bar to total > 40 at attempt 5, versus >=46 for a phase and >=42 for a chunk, and the only guard on reaching attempt 5 is verify_attempt_sequence. Four invocation failures (e.g. repeated launch_error or timeout, each of which writes a receipt from the tool's own prompt/check hashes) therefore unlock a 41/50 phase acceptance after a single real review. tools/test_management_phases.py:213-237 covers consumption and tamper detection but no test asserts anything about the fifth-attempt exception after failed attempts, and docs/PHASES.md:157-169 documents consumption without stating its effect on the exception.
findings.required_fix: Make the fifth-attempt exception depend on substantive review history: in gate_decision or its caller, require a minimum number of prior attempts with real completed records (for example at least three non-failed attempts) before allowing "accepted_with_deficiencies", keep failed receipts as budget consumption only, add a regression test that a fifth attempt preceded only by failed receipts is rejected at total 41, and state the rule in docs/PHASES.md:157-169.

findings.description: SCOPE_BOUND_PHASES is a literal frozenset({20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25}) rather than being derived from check_phase.MANAGEMENT_PHASES (check_phase.py:71). The attempt-01 finding asked for a single constant and the four duplicated literals are indeed gone (now lines 256, 446, 511, 576), but the two sources of truth can still drift: a phase 26 added to MANAGEMENT_PHASES would get a management gate and a contracts receipt while silently losing prompt scope binding, review_scope recording and declared-scope verification. No test asserts MANAGEMENT_PHASES is a subset of SCOPE_BOUND_PHASES.
findings.required_fix: Derive the set (for example SCOPE_BOUND_PHASES = frozenset({20, *check_phase.MANAGEMENT_PHASES}) with the import kept local to avoid the existing circular import, or assert the subset relation in tools/test_management_phases.py so divergence fails fast).

findings.description: The prompt emits two different "Active follow-up plan" lines: line 455 prints status["active_followup_plan"] (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md) and line 470 prints phases[phase].get("plan", "docs/implementation-plan.md"), which for phase 21 falls back to the generic plan. Both appear in this attempt's preserved prompt (docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-phase-governance-attempt-02.prompt.md:14 and :18), telling the reviewer two different governing plans for the same review. The prompt is hash-bound evidence, so the ambiguity is permanently recorded.
findings.required_fix: Either set an explicit "plan" key on phases 21-25 in docs/phase-status.json, or drop the line 470 fallback when active_followup_plan is already printed, so each prompt names one governing plan.

findings.description: verify_planning_fixture compares parsed JSON values, not bytes, after popping provenance.sha256/manifestSha256, while commands_for(21) excludes the file from the frozen diff (check_phase.py:126). A reindented or key-reordered crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/model-regressions.json would therefore pass the gate even though it ships inside the published crate source. docs/PHASES.md:179-184 accurately scopes the claim to "every other JSON value", so this is a narrowing of the byte freeze rather than an inaccurate document, but the packaged bytes are no longer pinned for that one file.
findings.required_fix: Rebuild the expected bytes instead of comparing dicts: re-serialise the baseline object with the rebound hash using the same formatting the generator emits and assert equality against the file's bytes, or assert that the only byte-level difference from the baseline blob is the 64-character hash substring.

evidence: docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-phase-governance-attempt-02.checks.json records 23 checks whose command list equals commands_for(21) element for element and in order (frozen-SDK diff with the planning-fixture exclusion, verify_planning_fixture, untracked-SDK assertion, the ten shared management commands, test_ci.py, model_fixtures/generate_constants/response_defaults --check, verify_native_fixtures --require-test-bindings, red_team_dataplane --check --require-complete, schema-oracle.mts, verify-gateway-specimens.mts, generate_validation --check, generate_models --check); every exit_code is 0, every timeout is false, passed and source_unchanged are true, and source_sha256 a428384348e68444253f18eec63e57f692bb787c1af4700264f8ec243f5feca4 equals the reviewed hash in this attempt's prompt (line 16).

docs/checks/phase-21.json:2-6 carries the identical phase, source hash, checked_at 2026-10-19T12:47:54.748250+00:00 and passed flag, consistent with the attempt snapshot being a byte copy taken by review_phase.py:450-453.

Attempt-01 finding 1 fixed and tested: tools/check_phase.py:108 adds vendor_scope to both hygiene commands for all management phases, lines 155-159 append it to inherited phase-19/20 hygiene commands, and tools/test_management_phases.py:70-74 asserts the exclusion in every `git diff ... --check` command for phases 21-25; the recorded run shows both commands executing with the exclusion (checks entries 4 and 5).

Attempt-01 finding 2 fixed: review_phase.check_evidence now requires report.get("scope") is None (tools/review_phase.py:200), and tools/test_management_phases.py:118-133 writes a contracts-only report for each of phases 21-25 and asserts check_evidence raises "incomplete". The test is sensitive for phase 21 because ci_commands_for(21) is still byte-identical to commands_for(21), so the scope marker is the only rejection path.

Attempt-01 finding 3 fixed: tools/check_phase.py:132-140 adds test_ci.py and every manifest-consuming generator/oracle, and tools/test_management_phases.py:76-82 pins them. The deliberate exclusion of tools/native_exports.py is justified and tested (test_plan_retains_static_closure_without_claiming_current_live_proof, lines 84-97): native_exports.py builds and compiles an external consumer crate (tools/native_exports.py:480-525) and reads crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml rather than contracts/manifest.json, so it is live/compile evidence deferred to phases 23-24, not a manifest consumer.

Attempt-01 finding 4 fixed: tools/test_management_phases.py:164-197 builds a complete record (prompt with the scope lines, cli envelope whose structured_output equals the review, and a checks snapshot matching commands_for(21)) and asserts verify_record is True at score 9 and False at score 8.5 with total 50, plus gate_decision(..., phase=21) == "rejected"; deleting the floor at review_phase.py:70 now breaks the test.

Attempt-01 findings 5 and 6 fixed: review_phase.py:523-529 writes a sanitized .failed.json for timeout/process_error/invalid_output/launch_error, verify_attempt_sequence accepts it as a consumed attempt with identity plus prompt/checks hash verification (lines 93-105), tools/test_management_phases.py:213-237 exercises all four reasons and tamper detection, and docs/PHASES.md:157-176 documents the recovery procedure and states explicitly that contracts-only routing is "not remote CI coverage for phases21–23".

Attempt-01 finding 7 fixed: SCOPE_BOUND_PHASES replaces the four duplicated literals (review_phase.py:17, used at 256, 446, 511, 576), gate_decision takes phase and applies the plan floor before the rubric (lines 69-71) so decision, gate_passed and the recorded status agree, and tools/test_management_phases.py:199-211 asserts verify_record rejects a phase-21 chunk record with a tampered review_scope, mismatched scope_evidence, or a rewritten prompt scope line even after rehashing the prompt.

The new frozen-SDK exception is tightly bounded: verify_planning_fixture (check_phase.py:79-102) pops exactly provenance.sha256 from both sides and compares the whole object, rejects symlinks, resolves the corpus path from the baseline object (so "source" cannot be redirected), requires the rebound hash to equal the actual contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json bytes, and requires that corpus to differ from baseline only by provenance.manifestSha256, which must equal the current contracts/manifest.json bytes. crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/model-regressions.json:4-12 confirms the declared source and hash fields, and tools/test_management_phases.py:29-68 proves specimen, schemaVersion, baselineCommit, generatorSha256, source, stale-hash and corpus mutations all raise.

Fail-closed later milestones re-verified at current source: tools/red_team_management.py:351-355 restricts --require-through-phase to 21-25 and raises unconditionally above 21, check_phase.py:143 adds that flag to every phase 22-25 list, test_management_phases.py:99-110 asserts it plus the absence of 0.2.2/phase-19/phase-20 receipt reuse, and test_red_team_management's test_future_phase_cannot_pass_on_plan_artifacts ran green in the recorded stderr (19 tests OK).

Private-material evidence is fresh and source-bound: docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json:3-12 records sourceSha256 a4283843..., headCommit 0a213fe79c..., passed true, 1871 git-visible files and zero selected-value matches at 12:47:26, 28 seconds before the gate run, and the --check output in the snapshot reports receiptFresh true with privateScanReexecuted false, matching its documented receipt-freshness-only semantics (limitations[4] of the receipt).

The high finding is verified from three independent artifacts: contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/mp-openapi.yaml has 46 lines matching [ \t]+$; docs/checks/phase-20-contracts.json:9-17 shows the b65f3c9..HEAD whitespace check as the first command actually executed by the contracts subset; and docs/CI.md:141-146 enumerates only the Portkey and dp-openapi.yaml exclusions while docs/CI.md:162-164 confirms the 41-command CI subset drops only Rust, package, native-export, candidate-guard and verify-fixtures commands.

Phase registration is complete and ordered: docs/phase-status.json:3 active_phase 21, :5018-5078 phase 21 with scope_evidence and two named chunks whose phase-governance scope (:5050-5055) matches this prompt's line 36 exactly, phases 22-25 each registered with nonempty chunk scopes, final_in_sequence on 25, and test_phases_registered_with_nonempty_scopes_and_order (test_management_phases.py:239-248) verifies ordered advancement against the real file.

docs/PHASES.md:133-139 declares the phase-21 milestones and required evidence, including the >=9/10 plan floor and the model-regressions exception, and lines 88-98 state the 42/46 and attempt-five >40 thresholds implemented in review_phase.gate_decision:79-86; docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:178-188 and 240-243 state the same scope and thresholds, and docs/implementation-plan.md:174-183 records the same phase 21-25 framing.
limitations: Read-only review: I executed nothing and could not recompute SHA-256 values, so the reviewed source hash a4283843..., the checks snapshot hash ba58cd03... and all check outcomes are judged from the preserved prompt, the recorded report and the source of the tools that produced them.

I could not run git, so the high finding is a prediction verified by inspection rather than by executing the failing command: the 46 trailing-whitespace lines, the new-file status of the vendored YAML (staged additions in the working tree), the command's presence in the executed CI subset and the two existing exclusions for the same situation together establish it, but the actual nonzero exit will only be observable after the commit exists in b65f3c9..HEAD.

docs/checks/ and docs/reviews/ are excluded from the review fingerprint (review_phase.py:15-16), so record, prompt, cli-envelope and snapshot integrity rests on self-reported hashes inside those same unfingerprinted files; a consistently edited set cannot be detected here. This is pre-existing design, not introduced by this chunk.

Scope was the phase-governance chunk (docs/PHASES.md, tools/check_phase.py, tools/review_phase.py, tools/test_management_phases.py). I did not audit the plan-and-provenance artifacts (contracts/airs-*.json, the vendored 0.86.0 tree, tools/red_team_management.py internals, manifest ownership rules) beyond what the governance claims depend on, and I did not re-audit historical phase lists other than the inherited commands that phases 20-25 reuse.

Static governance evidence only. Nothing here certifies runtime behaviour, request construction, generated Rust correctness, live tenant acceptance or any remote CI outcome, and no claim is made about phase 22-25 readiness.

The recorded unit-test output is taken from the snapshot's captured stderr; I verified that the suites listed there match the suites the gate commands select and that discovery cannot silently pass (check_phase.require_nonempty_tests, invoked at check_phase.py:38), but I did not re-execute any test.
